transcript:
Meeting: Redwood x Skybridge - Marketplace Integration Tech Sync
Date: 2026-03-23 10:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Chris (Redwood SE), Dana (Redwood Product), Jamie (Redwood PE), Sofia (Skybridge PM), Ravi (Skybridge Infra), Liu (Skybridge Security), Markus (Marketplace Lead)

Summary/Toplines: quick run through of marketplace listing requirements, reference arch for private/VPC deployments, packaging options (terraform/helm/container images), billing/usage mapping, security controls and pilot timeline.

00:00 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Chris our SE and Jamie from partner eng. How's everyone doing?
00:12 Sofia (Skybridge): Good, thanks Alex. Excited to get this rolling. Markus, Ravi and Liu are on.
00:20 Markus (Skybridge): Morning. We want to make sure our marketplace listing process is smooth and that the ref arch for private deployments is documented.
00:30 Chris (Redwood): Great, we put together a checklist but we wanted to review your requirements; there are a few variants: hosted listing (Redwood hosted), dedicated reserved capacity for customers via Skybridge, and private VPC package for enterprise customers.
00:45 Ravi (Skybridge): For us the priority is the marketplace packaged bundle for our customers to quickly spin up Redwood in their tenant with the correct networking and RBAC. Also we need a clear billing integration so usage shows up in Skybridge billing.
01:05 Dana (Redwood): To add, we support a private deployment control plane option — SDKs and the same API surface — so the experience is consistent. That means your marketplace package should include the control plane connector + a preflight checklist.
01:25 Liu (Skybridge): Security is top. We need KMS integration, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, SSO via SAML, and the ability to pin models and control data retention.
01:40 Chris (Redwood): Yep, all that is possible. Quick note on terminology: our KV "cache" sometimes shows up in documents as KV "cash" in auto transcripts, sorry in advance — but we manage prefix caching and an optional shared cache for tenants.
01:55 Markus (Skybridge): Ha, noted. Can you show the ref arch?
02:05 Jamie (Redwood): I'll share screen — high level: marketplace bundle contains an IAAS template (Terraform/ARM), a Helm chart for k8s deployments, and an image manifest. For private deployments we have a connector component that runs in the customer VPC and talks back to the Redwood control plane over an outbound-only connection, optional mTLS.
02:35 Sofia (Skybridge): outbound-only is good for customers with inbound restrictions. Do you support direct peering for higher throughput?
02:45 Chris (Redwood): Yes, we support VPC peering and config for dedicated capacity. For very latency-sensitive offerings we recommend dedicated GPU pools that we provision via an API. That will require some configuration on your marketplace to expose instance type choices.
03:05 Ravi (Skybridge): About the billing mapping — how do we map usage? We need an event stream or usage file that ties to Skybridge account ids.
03:18 Dana (Redwood): We have a usage events API that pushes per-token and per-embedding usage with timestamps and customer metadata. For marketplace we can send batched usage to your billing ingestion or provide an S3 export. We should confirm the fields you need (account id, SKU, units consumed).
03:38 Markus (Skybridge): S3 export with a unique mapping table would work. We'll share the schema we expect.
03:45 Liu (Skybridge Security): On KMS, do you integrate with external HSMs? We need key custody options.
03:52 Jamie (Redwood): We support customer-managed KMS keys and an HSM-backed flow for encryption at rest; we also provide key rotation hooks and audit logs. There are some region restrictions for HSM providers, we'll surface that in the reference arch doc.
04:12 Alex (Redwood): One thing to highlight — marketplace listings often require a short evaluation period and a pilot SKU. We usually recommend a 30-day pilot with constrained quota and an upgrade path.
04:25 Sofia (Skybridge): That fits our go-to-market; can we get a sample contract and SLA language for dedicated capacity?
04:34 Alex (Redwood): Absolutely, I'll loop in legal. We'll send sample T&Cs and SLA bullets.
04:42 Chris (Redwood): On the infra side, a few tech points: network egress, NAT, and bandwidth — for heavy inference customers you want peering or dedicated throughput. Also for model variants we can publish performance profiles so customers pick the right SKU.
05:02 Ravi (Skybridge): Performance profiles — can you share typical QPS and latency numbers for the models we plan to list (gpt-like 7B, 13B variants)?
05:12 Chris (Redwood): We'll share a perf sheet. Roughly for a 7B quantized profile on A100-like infra you can expect 40-60ms p50 for short prompts, but that varies. We'll include the exact numbers in the benchmark doc.
05:30 Markus (Skybridge): We also need a reference arch for air-gapped or on-prem customers. How mature is that offering?
05:38 Dana (Redwood): We have an on-prem package that includes air-gap install scripts and an optional private control plane that runs in the customer's network. For those we require a concierge install process and support contract.
05:55 Liu (Skybridge Security): For compliance customers, what certifications do you have? SOC2 Type II was mentioned earlier in your one-pager.
06:04 Alex (Redwood): Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II and working on ISO. We'll share our security pack with attestations.
06:12 Liu (Skybridge): Good. Please highlight encryption in transit, KMS, and audit log retention for the marketplace listing.
06:20 Jamie (Redwood): Will do. We'll add a dedicated security section in the ref arch.
06:25 Sofia (Skybridge): Operationally, what's the upgrade path? If a customer upgrades from hosted to dedicated we need clear migration steps.
06:34 Chris (Redwood): We support model/route pinning and a migration guide. It involves snapshotting KV cache where possible, re-pointing DNS or peering, and a canary rollout. We'll include a migration checklist.
06:50 Markus (Skybridge): On the marketplace side — listing metadata, logos, trial terms — do you have a standard assets pack?
06:58 Alex (Redwood): Yes, we'll provide an assets pack (logos, product description, short feature bullets) and sample screenshots from the Redwood Console.
07:10 Ravi (Skybridge): For the pilot benchmark: what's the minimum dataset? We want repeatable results — can you give a script?
07:18 Jamie (Redwood): We'll provide a benchmark harness — a script that runs X requests/sec with a specified prompt set and records p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. We'll also include a sample dataset and the expected environment variables.
07:34 Sofia (Skybridge): Timeline — can we aim to have the packaging artifacts and runbook by next Tuesday (2026-03-30)?
07:42 Alex (Redwood): Yes that's reasonable. We'll prioritize the packaging checklist and Terraform/Helm templates.
07:50 
10:12 -- mid-call more detailed technical back-and-forth --
10:20 Ravi (Skybridge): Networking detail: customers sometimes have strict egress rules; how does the connector handle TLS cert rotation?
10:28 Chris (Redwood): The connector uses mTLS and has automated cert rotation via the control plane. Latest certs are pulled out-of-band; we provide a small cert management utility in the helm chart.
10:44 Liu (Skybridge): Does that require any inbound ports?
10:48 Chris (Redwood): No, it's outbound only in default config. For peering we can open internal routes.
11:05 Markus (Skybridge): Marketplace compliance: what about data residency tags? Some customers require that inference happen in a specific region.
11:13 Dana (Redwood): We support region pinning and can provision capacity in specified regions; the marketplace listing must include region availability options.
11:24 Sofia (Skybridge): Any gotchas for the Skybridge catalog submission process?
11:28 Markus (Skybridge): We need the package, a short description, support contact, and a reference arch PDF. Also we validate the deploy script in a staging account.
11:38 Jamie (Redwood): We'll be happy to run the staging validation with you — provide us a test account and we'll run the helm deploy and smoke tests.
11:50 Alex (Redwood): Action items recap coming at the end — but one more: versioning. How will we present model upgrades in the marketplace?
11:58 Chris (Redwood): We'll expose model versioning in the listing metadata and allow customers to pin to a version. Our rollback is supported at the route layer.
12:10 
20:00 -- more discussion, some cross talk and fillers, transcript shows natural speech --
20:15 Sofia (Skybridge): Legal — who on your side handles the marketplace MSA?
20:20 Alex (Redwood): I'll introduce our partnerships counsel, that'll be in the next email.
20:30 
30:00 -- nearing end, recap and next steps --
30:05 Alex (Redwood): Recap: Redwood to send packaging checklist, terraform/helm samples, assets pack, security pack, perf benchmark harness. Skybridge to share billing schema, staging account for validation, and legal contact. Pilot demo week of 2026-03-30.
30:28 Markus (Skybridge): Sounds good. We also want a short joint solution one-pager for marketing once pilot is green.
30:35 Dana (Redwood): We'll draft a joint solution one-pager after the pilot and alignment on messaging.
30:45 Sofia (Skybridge): Ok let's lock the follow-up — propose Tue 2026-03-31 10am PT for a demo.
30:55 Alex (Redwood): I'll send a calendar invite.
31:00 
56:50 Alex (Redwood): Thanks everyone, appreciate the time. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
56:58 Ravi (Skybridge): Thanks all.
57:02 Meeting end.
